purpose: Compare quantity loss and output link with B as a fresh joint-training control; do not change backbone or time likelihood in this factorial.

observations: Intermittent Q lowers log-MSE and MAE but raises raw RMSE relative to J.
Taxi quantity degradation is concentrated in non-extreme quantity groups; a universal upward calibration is not justified.
Instacart large-quantity errors offset improvements in smaller quantities; the overall difference is small.
basis.interpretation: These are descriptive fixed-checkpoint J/Q results, not evidence that a proposed objective or output link improves generalization.

definitions.mu: mean(log1p(y)) over all original train rows, preserving B initialization population
definitions.original_link: qhat=expm1(softplus(z)); preserve original tensor operations, do not substitute exp(z)
definitions.log_original_loss: mse_loss(softplus(z), log1p(y.clamp_min(0)), reduction=none); negative observed targets rejected before this compatibility arithmetic
definitions.raw_scale: s=max(1, sqrt(mean(y^2))) over canonical next-event train targets, distinct from all-row population
definitions.joint_loss: legacy_time_loss + quantity_loss; arithmetic sample mean over one target per sequence; lambda_quantity=1
definitions.calibration: mu>0 and finite q0,z0,s>=1 required; no silent epsilon repair; both links at z0 have qhat=q0 and dqhat/dz=q0
definitions.limits: Initial curvature differs (original q0, softplus q0*log(2)); matching parameter count and initial slope does not imply identical function families or optimization.

controls.training_objective: joint for every case; these are not J/Q/T arms
controls.time_head: B legacy_clamped_rmtpp, intercept cap300 and wd cap10, unchanged in all quantity cases
controls.time_metric_name: legacy clamped time loss, not normalized Time NLL
controls.initialization: one fresh B state per dataset/seed, zero quantity-head weight and bias z0; clone full state and RNG for all four cases
controls.paired_training: same train targets, epoch permutations, batch hashes, RNG schedule, optimizer hyperparameters, steps and trainable parameter names/count
controls.input_and_causality: same B encoder/input transform; hide target quantity and disable target memory write; predict from preceding valid state; ignore padding
controls.loss_scale_caveat: Constant train-only s preserves the raw-MSE minimizer for a quantity-only objective but changes time/quantity weighting and global clipping in joint training. Contrasts include that optimization effect.
controls.gradient_measurement: record task-specific encoder/head norms, joint preclip norm and actual clip factor on matched train batches; zero initial encoder quantity gradient makes initial norm-ratio calibration inapplicable

primary_selector.ties: strict improvement only; earliest epoch wins

secondary_selector.ties: strict improvement only; earliest epoch wins

evaluation.matched_step: report all cases at common final epoch120/global step separately from best-selector results
evaluation.same_checkpoint: report RMSE, MAE and time loss at the quantity-selected checkpoint together; never merge independent selector optima

binning.missing_cells: zero count and null metrics; no invented zeros
binning.boundary_policy: Reuse the pinned diagnosis boundaries verbatim; do not refit or choose boundaries on validation.

evaluation.interaction: raw_softplus - raw_original - log_softplus + B_log_original, computed separately for each dataset and metric
interpretation_limits: Best-selector contrasts measure the complete train-and-select procedure, not same-step effects.
Conditioning on true quantity does not alone establish prediction calibration error.
History cells are descriptive and may be confounded with quantity or series composition.
No pooling of raw-unit errors across datasets.
Single-seed validation cannot establish benchmark superiority.
evaluation.pilot_decision: Use per-dataset changes and all tradeoffs to narrow one common recipe. A universal quantity-improvement candidate must lower raw RMSE versus B in all three datasets; otherwise retain B as control and describe dataset dependence. This is a descriptive pilot gate, not a significance threshold or a claim of joint time/quantity superiority.

time_head_review.finding: J and T both show late validation deterioration concentrated in long intervals; neither quantity interference nor clamp alone is established as the cause.
time_head_review.taxi_observation_law: positive integer lognormal PMF: d=1 uses P(T<=1.5); d>=2 uses P(d-0.5<T<=d+0.5); float64 stable CDF/survival differences with no probability or loss cap
time_head_review.assumption: The latent continuous-to-integer observation model is a modeling choice, not an observed preprocessing fact.
time_head_review.existing_implementation_scope: frozen encoder and quantity head; detached hidden cache; 130 trainable time parameters
time_head_review.recommendation: Reuse the normalized likelihood in a separate future fresh joint-training track after quantity comparison; do not duplicate the existing frozen-head refit.
integration_gaps: time_scale_weight.weight must belong to time_head group, not encoder
future_acceptance: strict earliest selectors and exact resume
quantity guardrail at a common checkpoint
time_head_review.metric_compatibility: Do not subtract legacy clamped score from normalized PMF NLL or inherit the old +0.01 threshold for the new likelihood.

implementation.state: numerical primitive and causal joint-batch objective implemented; full training/evaluation/resume runner not implemented
implementation.identity_scope: case/mu/raw_scale serialize and reject mismatches; source/data/runtime/batch schedule/checkpoint identity must be bound by the future execution runner
